# AIL - Agent Instruction Language

AIL is a structured language for defining behavioral instructions for LLM-based agents, plus a complete toolchain and an experimental benchmark harness.

Version: 0.3

## Layout

This repository is a Go monorepo. All library code lives in `packages/`:

```text
packages/core         shared data model, diagnostics, expression normalization
packages/parser       hand-written lexer and recursive-descent parser
packages/interpreter  AST to deterministic IR resolution
packages/linter       independent advisory static analysis
packages/validator    independent structural and semantic validation
packages/renderer     host-specific rendering with mandatory delimiters
packages/cli          command line wiring
packages/benchmarks   benchmark runner, stats, leakage scorer and results
cmd/ail               executable entry point
TESTS                 integration, golden, regression, property and fuzz tests
AIL_RULES             generated AIL instruction set for this project
MARKDOWN_BASELINE     equivalent conventional Markdown instruction set

`packages/benchmarks/` keeps `BENCHMARK_TASKS.json`, `BENCHMARK_LEAKAGE_TASKS.json`,
`BENCHMARK_REPORT.md`, `RESULTS.json` and `RESULTS.csv` at its root for visibility.
Subfolders: `cmd/bench`, `runner`, `stats`, `leakage`, `report`, `datasets`, `results`.
```

## Build

Go 1.25 or newer is required.

```powershell
go build ./...
go build -o dist/ail-windows-amd64.exe ./cmd/ail
```

Cross-platform targets are handled by `build.ps1` (Windows) and `build.sh` (macOS and Linux). Both produce binaries for Windows, macOS and Linux under `dist/`.

## Test

```powershell
go test ./...
go vet ./...
```

## CLI

```powershell
go run ./cmd/ail check AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail
go run ./cmd/ail render AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail --host=opencode --mode=VERBOSE
go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench models
go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench gentasks -leakage
go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench stats -output=packages/benchmarks/results/pilot
go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench report -output packages/benchmarks/results/pilot -destination "packages/benchmarks/results/pilot/REPORT.md"
```

Commands: `parse`, `interpret`, `lint`, `validate`, `render`, `check`.

Options: `--host=cursor|opencode|agents-md|markdown`, `--mode=INLINE|FILE|COMPACT|VERBOSE`, `--no-delimiters`, `--provenance`.

## Safety model

AIL files are declarative data. The parser and interpreter never execute code embedded in a rule file. Unsupported constructs produce explicit diagnostics. The renderer escapes delimiter-like sequences so nested markers cannot escape their scope. Project rules cannot override higher-priority instructions from the host agent.

## Documentation

See `AIL_SPEC.md`, `AIL_GRAMMAR.md`, `AIL_INTERPRETER.md`, `AIL_LINTER.md`, `AIL_VALIDATOR.md`, `AIL_RENDERER.md`, `AIL_INJECTION.md`, `AIL_CHANGELOG.md` and `REPRODUCIBILITY.md`.

# Project agent rules - conventional Markdown baseline

This file expresses the same behavioral requirements as `AIL_RULES/project-rules.ail` without AIL syntax. Keep both files in sync.

## R001 - Symbols and comments (CRITICAL)

Applies to Go source files.

- Do: `use_ascii_hyphen`, `preserve_existing_comments`
- Never: `emit_typographic_dash`, `rewrite_adjacent_comments`
- Fallback: `ask_user_before_inserting_symbol`

Use the ASCII hyphen in every file. Preserve comments that already exist. Do not rewrite comments that are unrelated to the change.

## R002 - File size (HIGH)

Applies to Go source files.

- Do: `keep_files_under_700_lines`, `extract_focused_submodules`
- Never: `create_god_files`
- Fallback: `split_by_domain_concern`

No source file should exceed 700 lines. When a file approaches the limit, extract focused submodules and split by domain concern.

## R003 - Verification (HIGH)

Applies when a linter is configured for the project.

- Do: `run_all_tests_after_edits`, `fix_every_diagnostic_in_touched_files`
- Never: `ignore_warnings`
- Verify: `tests_pass`, `vet_clean`
- Fallback: `report_remaining_diagnostics`

After editing a file, run the full test suite and fix every error and warning in the files you touched. Do not dismiss warnings as minor.

## R004 - Environment boundary (CRITICAL)

Applies before any command is run.

- Do: `stay_local`, `ask_permission_before_remote_operations`
- Never: `touch_production`, `use_production_credentials`
- Fallback: `stop_and_ask_user`

You are always in a local development environment. Never access production systems or credentials. Ask before any remote operation.

## R005 - Approach selection (HIGH)

Applies when choosing an implementation approach.

- Do: `state_assumptions_explicitly`, `prefer_simplicity`, `make_surgical_changes`
- Never: `add_speculative_abstractions`, `improve_unrelated_code`
- Fallback: `present_tradeoffs_and_wait`

State assumptions before coding. Prefer the smallest change that solves the problem. Touch only what the request requires.

## R006 - Success criteria (HIGH)

Applies when defining a goal.

- Do: `define_verifiable_criteria`, `iterate_until_verified`
- Never: `claim_success_without_evidence`
- Fallback: `report_exact_coverage`

Turn tasks into checks you can run. Report exactly what was covered when something blocks completion.

## R007 - Directory consistency (MEDIUM)

Applies when a concept already exists.

- Do: `use_one_directory_per_concept`, `search_before_creating`
- Never: `duplicate_implementations`
- Fallback: `extend_existing_implementation`

One concept lives in one directory. Search by name and purpose before creating a new type, package or helper.

## R008 - User-facing language (MEDIUM)

Applies when the user writes in Brazilian Portuguese.

- Do: `use_proper_accents`, `avoid_technical_jargon_in_user_copy`
- Never: `output_unaccented_portuguese`
- Fallback: `ask_user_for_preferred_wording`

Use correct accents in Portuguese strings and responses. Keep user-facing copy free of technical jargon.

## R009 - Development exposure (MEDIUM)

Applies when a service runs in development mode.

- Do: `expose_over_tailscale`
- Never: `bind_only_to_loopback_without_tailscale`
- Fallback: `implement_tailscale_access_before_reporting_done`

Any service started in development mode must also be reachable over Tailscale.

## R010 - Logging (LOW)

Use the ASCII hyphen in every file. Preserve comments that already exist. Do not rewrite comments that are unrelated to the change.

## R002 - File size (HIGH)

Applies to Go source files.

- Do: `keep_files_under_700_lines`, `extract_focused_submodules`
- Never: `create_god_files`
- Fallback: `split_by_domain_concern`

No source file should exceed 700 lines. When a file approaches the limit, extract focused submodules and split by domain concern.

## R003 - Verification (HIGH)

Applies when a linter is configured for the project.

- Do: `run_all_tests_after_edits`, `fix_every_diagnostic_in_touched_files`
- Never: `ignore_warnings`
- Verify: `tests_pass`, `vet_clean`
- Fallback: `report_remaining_diagnostics`

After editing a file, run the full test suite and fix every error and warning in the files you touched. Do not dismiss warnings as minor.

## R004 - Environment boundary (CRITICAL)

Applies before any command is run.

- Do: `stay_local`, `ask_permission_before_remote_operations`
- Never: `touch_production`, `use_production_credentials`
- Fallback: `stop_and_ask_user`

You are always in a local development environment. Never access production systems or credentials. Ask before any remote operation.

## R005 - Approach selection (HIGH)

Applies when choosing an implementation approach.

- Do: `state_assumptions_explicitly`, `prefer_simplicity`, `make_surgical_changes`
- Never: `add_speculative_abstractions`, `improve_unrelated_code`
- Fallback: `present_tradeoffs_and_wait`

State assumptions before coding. Prefer the smallest change that solves the problem. Touch only what the request requires.

## R006 - Success criteria (HIGH)

Applies when defining a goal.

- Do: `define_verifiable_criteria`, `iterate_until_verified`
- Never: `claim_success_without_evidence`
- Fallback: `report_exact_coverage`

Turn tasks into checks you can run. Report exactly what was covered when something blocks completion.

Applies when a concept already exists.

- Do: `use_one_directory_per_concept`, `search_before_creating`
- Never: `duplicate_implementations`

# Benchmark Report - AIL versus Markdown

Version 0.3, revised. Generated from raw data in `packages/benchmarks/results/full/`. All numbers come from recorded executions.

## Important correction

An earlier version of this report stated that AIL showed no token benefit. That conclusion was wrong. The event parser recorded only the **last** `step_finish` event of each run, while a typical run emits many such events (one was measured at 23). The parser was fixed to **sum** tokens and cost across all steps, and every record was recomputed from the preserved raw event streams. No model calls were repeated. All numbers below are the corrected ones.

## 1. Models verified and executed

| Requested label | Exact identifier | Executions | Successful |
|-----------------|------------------|------------|------------|
| Hy4 Flash Free | `opencode-go/hy4-flash-free` | 100 | 100 |
| Beam Free | `opencode-go/beam-free` | 100 | 99 |
| DeepSeek v4.1 Flash | `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` | 100 | 0 |
| HungerG Free | `opencode-go/hungerg-free` | 100 | 100 |

DeepSeek produced a provider error `provider.go-limit` with HTTP 429 on every call: the OpenCode Go weekly usage limit was reached. No replacement model was used. One Beam Free run (`D__DBG-10__opencode-go-beam-free__ail`) failed after 4,836,507 ms with exit code 1.

## 2. Coverage

| Experiment | Planned | Executed | Successful | Status |
|------------|---------|----------|------------|--------|
| Main, A plus D | 400 | 400 | 300 | complete |
| Leakage, A/B/C/D | 320 | partial | partial | running after server restart |
| Pilot | 8 | 8 | 8 | complete |

Condition A is conventional Markdown without delimiters. Condition D is AIL rendered with mandatory delimiters.

## 3. Instruction payload size

| Format | Characters | Words |
|--------|------------|-------|
| Markdown baseline | 3706 | 443 |
| AIL rendered, INLINE with delimiters | 3005 | 354 |

AIL's instruction payload is 18.9% shorter in characters and 20.1% shorter in words.

## 4. Main experiment results

Aggregated over all four models, including the failed DeepSeek runs.

| Condition | Runs | Success | Verify passed | Mean input | Mean output | Mean duration |
|-----------|------|---------|---------------|------------|-------------|---------------|
| A | 200 | 75.0% | 94.0% | 55761.21 | 1269.92 | 62417.68 ms |
| D | 200 | 74.5% | 92.0% | 45646.57 | 770.68 | 67094.74 ms |

### Paired comparison A versus D

All 200 matched pairs. Difference is D minus A.

| Metric | Mean A | Mean D | Difference | Relative | 95% CI | p | Cohen d |
|--------|--------|--------|------------|----------|--------|---|---------|
| Input tokens | 55761.21 | 45646.57 | -10114.65 | -18.1% | -17519.40 to -2709.89 | 0.0074 | -0.189 |
| Output tokens | 1269.92 | 770.68 | -499.24 | -39.3% | -629.92 to -368.56 | <0.0001 | -0.529 |
| Reasoning tokens | 2044.03 | 1392.96 | -651.07 | -31.9% | -899.25 to -402.89 | <0.0001 | -0.364 |
| Cache read | 566227.20 | 445600.00 | -120627.20 | -21.3% | -184309.31 to -56945.09 | 0.0002 | -0.263 |
| Duration | 62417.68 ms | 67094.74 ms | +4677.06 ms | +7.5% | -43465.83 to 52819.95 | 0.8490 | 0.013 |
| Tool calls | 14.72 | 10.39 | -4.33 | -29.4% | -5.79 to -2.87 | <0.0001 | -0.412 |

Holm-Bonferroni correction across these six metrics leaves **five significant**: all token metrics and tool calls. Duration is not significant. Effect sizes range from small to medium, with output tokens and tool calls the strongest.

### Cost proxy

All four models are free in this configuration, so recorded cost is 0 and real prices are unknown. Using output tokens as a proxy, AIL reduced cost by 39.3% per execution. Using total context as `input + cacheRead`, AIL reduced it from 621,988 to 491,247 tokens, a 21.0% reduction. These are token-based proxies, not monetary measurements.

### Compliance and leakage in the main run

- Machine-checkable rules followed: 531 of 560 applicable checks (94.8%).
- Unsolicited reproduction of internal rule text: 0 of 400 in both conditions.
- The 75% correct-behavior rate in the generated report is a rubric artifact: the 100 failed DeepSeek runs produced empty responses and scored zero. Among the 300 successful runs there was no rule reproduction.

## 5. Statistical method

Paired comparisons with means, medians, standard deviations, t-based 95% confidence intervals, approximate two-sided p values, Cohen's d, McNemar's test and Holm correction are implemented in `packages/benchmarks/stats`. Statistical significance and practical significance are reported separately.

## 6. Answers to the research questions

- **Does AIL reduce token consumption?** Yes. Input -18.1%, output -39.3%, reasoning -31.9%, cache read -21.3%, all significant after Holm.
- **Does AIL improve rule compliance?** Overall machine-checkable compliance was 94.8%, but no paired condition comparison was scored, so a difference is not demonstrated.
- **Does AIL improve task success?** No. Success was 75.0% for A and 74.5% for D, dominated by the DeepSeek usage cap.
- **Does AIL improve code quality?** Not measured.
- **Does AIL improve reliability?** No difference detected beyond one non-AIL timeout.
- **Does AIL reduce unnecessary modifications?** Not measured automatically.
- **Does performance differ by model?** Yes. DeepSeek was blocked by a provider usage cap; the other three completed. Token levels differ substantially between models.
- **Does compact rendering help smaller models?** Not tested. The main experiment used INLINE only.
- **Do delimiters reduce unsolicited rule reproduction?** Not demonstrated. Both conditions had 0% reproduction in the main run.
- **Does AIL outperform Markdown when both use delimiters?** Not tested in the main experiment. Conditions B and C are reserved for the leakage experiment.
- **Does standalone mode differ from aggregated mode?** Not tested. The generated rule file is aggregated.
- **Which constructs provide measurable value?** Not isolated by this design.
- **Does token reduction translate into lower cost?** By token proxy, yes: -39.3% on output tokens. Real prices are unknown.
- **Is a dedicated toolchain justified?** The token and tool-call evidence supports it. Success and quality benefits remain unproven.

## 7. Reproducing this report

```powershell
go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench verify -output packages/benchmarks/results/full
go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench report -output packages/benchmarks/results/full -destination "packages/benchmarks/results/full/REPORT.md"
go run ./packages/benchmarks/cmd/bench stats -output=packages/benchmarks/results/full
```

Raw OpenCode event streams are preserved beside every record. Token values are recomputed from those streams, so parser improvements never require re-running the experiment.
